office: the National Organization for Civil Registration (NOCR), through post offices and Pishkhan service centres

routes.label: registered online, then in person at a post office or Pishkhan centre; personalised centrally in Tehran

note: Landinfo's report on Iranian documents (5 January 2021): every citizen over 15 must hold the kart-e melli, now only issued as an electronic smart card by the NOCR; the applicant registers online, pays a registration fee and books an appointment at one of some 5,000 offices. The fee's amount, the card's term and the time aren't stated, and the NOCR's site is unstable, so they're null.

sources.title: Landinfo (Norwegian Country of Origin Information Centre), Iran: Passports, ID and civil status documents (5 January 2021), on ecoi.net
sources.said: Iran has introduced a national ID card, kart-e melli, which all Iranian citizens over 15 years shall be in possession of ... Currently only the electronic version of the kart-e melli is issued in Iran ... as well as pay a registration fee and print out the form they have filled out during the online registration.
